thesis: Reflective societies may make continuation harder, but observed counterexamples defeat a simple triumph of harmful traits.
role: Present provocative question then reverse caricature.

ideas.statement: The reproductive costs of prudence depend on social environments.
Biological persistence does not establish moral worth.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Male cognition and conscientiousness examples contradict universal decline narratives.
Disease-risk/fertility associations illustrate trade-offs, not disease being good.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Genetic implications require transmissibility and persistent context; the starting society is imagined.

audit.notes: Entire assigned batch read; numbered subchapters covered; no independent citation verification.
